They compare their approach against a range of baseline anomaly detection methods, demonstrating that their likelihood-based approach performs competitively. The paper also includes a theoretical analysis, supported by visualizations and statistical analysis, to further understand the phenomenon and its implications. The authors argue that the success of likelihood-based anomaly detection in tabular data can be attributed to the fact that tabular data often has a lower intrinsic dimensionality and weaker feature correlations compared to images, making it easier for normalizing flows to learn a meaningful data representation. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the behavior of deep generative models in different data domains and provides valuable insights into the applicability of likelihood-based anomaly detection for tabular data.
